screens.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE high-fidelity desktop software screen, wide landscape 16:10, edge-to-edge screenshot, no physical device, no desk. Product ANIMAL ATLAS is a musical instrument driven by real wildlife events. It has two dedicated screens, ATLAS and SOUND STUDIO, linked by a persistent top navigation and shared session/transport bar. This screen is part of a matched pair. Use generous desktop-readable controls and clear hierarchy, not a crowded generic dashboard. All data, geography, animals, sources and musical assignments are illustrative; small footer 'Illustrative data · Interface concept'. Never imply a stationary bird detection is an individual track. Avoid decorative unreadable microtext. Pair A · Observatory. Flat precision scientific design: midnight-navy background, slate-blue map land, restrained mint and coral highlights, ivory contemporary sans typography with small monospaced timestamps, hairline dividers. No hardware screws, wood or neon. Quiet, rigorous and elegant. SCREEN ONE — ATLAS. The selected top tab is ATLAS; adjacent SOUND STUDIO tab clearly available. The geographic map fills at least 75 percent of the usable workspace: large recognizable Pacific-centered world map including Australia and New Zealand, subtle bathymetry or geographic grid consistent with style, several sparse event ripples, fixed bird station circles and distinct shark satellite-fix diamonds. A tiny NZ regional inset is allowed, no globe. Right narrow live-event drawer contains 3-4 concise events with species, measurement type, source, observation age and last fetch separately; a selected event reads 'Tui / Acoustic detection / Station location / BirdWeather'. An illustrative shark fix is clearly labelled older, no false fast-moving shark animation. Map region selection outlines 'South Pacific' and a small label 'Region FX: Ocean Space', linking geography to the sound studio. Top persistent strip contains ANIMAL ATLAS, ATLAS / SOUND STUDIO tabs, session name 'Pacific Session', LIVE / REPLAY badge, record indicator and master audio meter. Bottom shallow transport has Record, Play, Stop, Loop, Observed / Arrival timeline mode, 60x replay speed and timeline. Keep sound-design knobs and patch editors out of the map workspace; only a small 'Edit selected voice' button links to studio. This is an expansive live listening atlas and event explorer.

Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE high-fidelity desktop software screen, wide landscape 16:10, edge-to-edge screenshot, no physical device, no desk. Product ANIMAL ATLAS is a musical instrument driven by real wildlife events. It has two dedicated screens, ATLAS and SOUND STUDIO, linked by a persistent top navigation and shared session/transport bar. This screen is part of a matched pair. Use generous desktop-readable controls and clear hierarchy, not a crowded generic dashboard. All data, geography, animals, sources and musical assignments are illustrative; small footer 'Illustrative data · Interface concept'. Never imply a stationary bird detection is an individual track. Avoid decorative unreadable microtext. Pair A · Observatory. Flat precision scientific design: midnight-navy background, slate-blue map land, restrained mint and coral highlights, ivory contemporary sans typography with small monospaced timestamps, hairline dividers. No hardware screws, wood or neon. Quiet, rigorous and elegant. SCREEN TWO — SOUND STUDIO. The selected top tab is SOUND STUDIO; ATLAS tab clearly available. This is the dedicated sound-design screen, not another big map. Top persistent strip identical in structure to the Atlas screen: ANIMAL ATLAS, ATLAS / SOUND STUDIO tabs, session 'Pacific Session', LIVE / REPLAY badge, record indicator and master meter. LEFT narrow animal/voice rack lists Tui, Great white shark, Humpback whale, Turtle, with mute/solo and miniature level; Tui selected. CENTER spacious selected-animal editor occupies half the screen: 'Tui · Acoustic detections' title, small source metadata, three contrasting voice-layer choices Pluck / Air / Resonance, a clear editable ADSR envelope, tuning/key/scale, filter and 4 large expressive controls Density, Tone, Decay, Motion. Below is a compact understandable mapping section Species → Pitch, Detection interval → Envelope, Station position → Pan; do not use fictitious bird movement speed. RIGHT region-effects rack titled 'REGION EFFECTS' includes a SMALL recognizable NZ/South Pacific region selector map used only for targeting, selected 'South Pacific', region membership badge, sends for Ocean Space reverb and Tidal Echo delay, wet/dry and decay/feedback controls, clear routing 'Animal voice → Region sends → Master' and overlap policy 'Highest-priority region'. Include a selected-event audition button and visible output trim, keep default headroom sensible. This must look like a real coherent professional sound-design workspace, not a grid of meaningless knobs. No giant map in this screen. The attached image is the matching ATLAS screen: preserve its palette, type system, top navigation, panel materials and bottom transport. Replace its main workspace with the SOUND STUDIO design described above. Do NOT produce another atlas map screen. Emphasize per-animal synthesis and independently targeted region effects.
